doc.name: TheStrat for agents
doc.instructions:
TheStrat tools. You bring OHLC bars; the tools return checkable facts in TheStrat words.
Do not read charts by eye: call these tools and quote their output.
Framing: TheStrat does not backtest patterns. It gathers evidence of participation by price and time.
Say facts ("SPY day: 2u, above the day open: buyers are more aggressive"), not opinions ("looks bullish").
Wording: distance from an open (and FTFC) is the level of aggression of buyers or sellers: who is more
willing to buy at higher prices or sell at lower prices. Describe it only as aggression.
Every signal carries a trigger, a target (magnitude) and a level of reclaim, plus source_url: cite it.
Order of work: describe_price (whole picture) -> find_signals (one timeframe) -> exhaustion (time left) ->
define_term / docs_search to explain a word. Many symbols at once (a sector ETF + holdings, or SPY QQQ DIA IWM):
sim_setups (before the break) -> sim_breaks (the break, same bar, 2+ symbols) -> sector_analysis. Bars: oldest first, each {t, o, h, l, c} with t = bar start
(ISO time, New York session 09:30-16:00). 60-minute bars start at 09:30.
A user's portfolio ("protect my assets"): prompt protect_portfolio, then portfolio_check. Report conditions
and evidence only, never an action ("buy", "sell", "hedge").

tools.description:
Label every bar as TheStrat scenario 1, 2u, 2d or 3 (Truth #1).

    Rule: compare each bar with the bar before it. Took the prior high only = 2u. Took the
    prior low only = 2d. Took both = 3. Took neither = 1 (inside bar). Equal to the prior
    high/low is NOT a take-out (still a 1). The first bar has no scenario (null).
    Also returns color, hammer/shooter shape, failed-2 flags (2u red / 2d green = potential 3)
    and 3u/3d when the bar has first_side data. Use this instead of reading a chart.

bars.description: OHLC bars, oldest first. Each bar is an object {t, o, h, l, c, v?} (also accepts open/high/low/close/time) or a row [t, o, h, l, c, v?]. t = bar START time, ISO 8601 (New York time if no offset). Daily bars may use a date only.
bars.title: Bars

tools.name: classify_bars

tools.description:
Full timeframe continuity (FTFC, Truth #2): is the last sale above (up) or below (down)
    the open of every timeframe in the group, or mixed (conflict)?

    Returns per-timeframe side, color and aggression (above an open: buyers more aggressive,
    willing to buy at higher prices; below: sellers more aggressive), state up/down/mixed,
    override (day and 60 agree against the week/month) and the profit-taking note (only the
    60 red). FTFC is a state, not a signal.

opens.description: Open price of the CURRENT bar per timeframe, e.g. {"M": 650.1, "W": 662.0, "D": 665.2, "60": 666.0}.
opens.title: Opens

group.description: standard = M W D 60 (default), intraday = 60 30 15 5, investing = Y Q M W, all = Y Q M W D 60 30 15 5.
group.title: Group

tools.name: timeframe_continuity

tools.description:
Find TheStrat actionable signals on one timeframe.

    Patterns: 2-2 reversal, 1-2-2 rev strat, 3-2-2, 2-1-2, 3-1-2, 3-2, hammer, shooter,
    momo hammer/shooter, inside bar, outside bar reversal (2d-3u / 2u-3d), 1-3 rev strat,
    1-3-2, I-O-I. Each signal has: trigger, target (magnitude, null if the pattern has
    none), level_of_reclaim, invalidation, status, sequence, kind (reversal/continuation)
    and source_url (the docs page for the rule).

    Status: setup (trigger not taken), in_force (taken, target not hit, still active),
    triggered (taken, bar closed, no target), hit_target, failed. Timing: a signal is in
    force only while its bar is open; D fires stay active until the next session open;
    the W is closed from Friday close to Monday open.

bars.description: OHLC bars, oldest first. Each bar is an object {t, o, h, l, c, v?} (also accepts open/high/low/close/time) or a row [t, o, h, l, c, v?]. t = bar START time, ISO 8601 (New York time if no offset). Daily bars may use a date only.
bars.title: Bars

tools.description:
Exhaustion risk: how much time is left in the signal's bar (session minutes,
    wall-clock minutes, sessions left, fraction left), and until when the fire stays active.

    Docs example: a 60-minute hammer that triggers at 9:32 has 58 minutes; at 10:25 it has 5.
    Once the bar closes, the signal is gone. The tool reports time; it does not grade it.

now.description: Current time, ISO 8601. Decides if the last bar is still open. Default: the server clock.
now.title: Now

tools.name: exhaustion

tools.description:
Multi-timeframe price analysis in plain language for one symbol (quant price action,
    technical signals, timeframe continuity) from your own bars.

    Returns `text` (one short line per timeframe, e.g. "SPY day: 2u, above the day open
    (green). Last 3 bars: 2d 1 2u. In force: bullish 2-1-2 ...") and the same facts as
    JSON: scenario, color, last 3 bars, signals in force, setups, and FTFC (M W D 60).
    Start here, then quote the text to the user. Hosted server: free, no cooldown.
    Fair-use limit: 60 calls per minute.

tools.description:
Simultaneous breaks: find which symbols in a basket broke their setup bar in the same
    direction in the same bar (2d-2u, 1-2u, 3-1-2u up / 2u-2d, 1-2d down). Quant price action
    and sector rotation from your own OHLC data, no third-party feed.

    Docs: "A simultaneous break is multiple correlated assets breaking 2 in the same direction
    at the same time." No threshold: the count and the % of the basket, ranked. At 80%+ the
    group gets the label "80%+ concentration: evidence of algorithmic buying (selling) in this
    group". Returns a ranked list per direction with count, % of basket,
    symbols, and per symbol the trigger, target and level of reclaim, plus the as-of time
    and a `text` line to quote.

tools.description:
Protect-your-assets check for one portfolio, from your own bars: measurable conditions on the
    losing side of the user's positions, with the evidence. Read the playbook first: MCP resource
    thestrat://playbooks/protect-portfolio (or the prompt protect_portfolio).

    Returns (1) the market condition: "Algorithmic buying identified in VIX while algorithmic selling in
    4 major indexes" (VIX symbol over its M W D 60 opens, SPY QQQ IWM DIA each under all 4), confirmed or
    not at a 60-minute close, plus the VIX futures curve state if given; (2) per position, the opens on
    the holder's losing side (long: under the open = buyers on that timeframe are losing; short: over the
    open = sellers are losing), reversals in force against the position (buy/sell list rule) and setups
    against it (trigger not taken), with trigger, target and level of reclaim; (3) concentration: the %
    of the user's basket (and of each ETF basket) whose current bar took the prior bar's low or high,
    labelled at 80%+. Each part has `text` to quote and source URLs. Conditions only: not a buy or sell
    signal. Quote `footer` at the end.

positions.description: The user's positions: {"NVDA": "long", "TSLA": "short"} or [{"symbol": "NVDA", "side": "long"}]. Up to 25. Sizes are not needed.
positions.title: Positions

bars_by_timeframe.description: Bars per timeframe, then per symbol: {"M": {"NVDA": [...], "VIXY": [...], "SPY": [...]}, "W": {...}, "D": {...}, "60": {...}}. Each position on the user's timeframes (investor Y; position trader Q M; swing or day trader W D 60). VIX or a VIX ETN (VIXY, VXX, UVXY) and SPY QQQ IWM DIA on M W D 60 for the market condition. The last bar of each timeframe must be the current bar (its open is the open). 60 symbols and 500 bars per symbol per timeframe; 10 to 50 bars are enough.
bars_by_timeframe.title: Bars By Timeframe
